setup.why: Confirm empirically, first-hand, that the custom-field collection is account/workspace-level with no project or workspace identifier anywhere in the request, before deciding create_custom_field is unsafe to probe (a created field cannot be scoped away from the rest of the account, and cannot be cleaned up since delete is destructive-refused).

produced.observation: Single flat collection of 30 rows, all sharing group_id 3452. The request itself accepts only pagination params (p, count) -- no project_id, no workspace_id, no PR-NNN, no path_params at all -- confirming the read side of this entity has no project/workspace scoping mechanism to read through, let alone write through.

contract.json_path: flat body (no nesting) plus optional array sub-objects: options[] ({option_value, is_default}), assigned_projects[] (PR-NNN strings), levels[] ({name, level_type, index}) for nested_dropdown, datasets[] ({linked_to_all_projects, linked_projects, unlinked_projects, link_to_future_projects, options}) for advanced use, and parent_custom_field_id (integer|null, key must be present for nested_dropdown tiers)

notes:
NOT INVOKED. This capability was never called, with any arguments -- zero attempts, by deliberate user safety decision, not a probing failure. Reason: custom_field is an account/workspace-level entity, not project- or workspace-scoped (confirmed above via setup[1], a real read-only call to list_custom_fields: the account's 30 custom fields are one flat collection, all sharing group_id 3452, and the request accepts no project/workspace identifier of any kind). A field created by this capability would land permanently in that same account-wide collection regardless of which projects were told to offer it. It cannot be removed afterward: the sibling delete_custom_field_definition is mode:destructive, and a separate sibling probe (see tests/live/runs/tm/delete_template.json for the same pattern on a different destructive capability) confirmed invokeCapability refuses destructive capabilities outright -- 'is a destructive operation and is not available through this surface' -- even when user_permission is set to 'granted'. So a create here would be permanent, unrecoverable account pollution with no undo path. The user's standing instruction for this batch is: when a capability is workspace-wide and uncleanable, mark it UNVERIFIED and document the contract rather than invoking it. That is what this record does.

Full declared contract from describeCapability (product tm, name create_custom_field), captured carefully since this is the main deliverable:
- Body is flat (no json_path body-root nesting) with these top-level fields: field_type (string, values: string, text, user, dropdown, multi_dropdown, url, boolean, int, date, nested_dropdown), field_name (string, 1-256 chars, trimmed before storage), is_required (boolean), place_holder_text (string, max 256), default_value (accepted by schema but not settable at create for any type), entity_type (values: TestCase only; default TestCase; anything else is 400 'Only TestCase entity type is supported'), options (array of {option_value (required, non-empty string), is_default (boolean)}), applies_to_all_projects (boolean, default false), assigned_projects (array of PR-NNN identifier strings, e.g. PR-12345), link_to_future_projects (boolean, default false), levels (array, min 2 entries, each {name, level_type, index}; required for nested_dropdown, ignored otherwise), parent_custom_field_id (integer >=1, nullable; key presence itself selects the nested-create path), datasets (array, advanced/forwarded-as-sent, {linked_to_all_projects, linked_projects (numeric ids, not PR-NNN), unlinked_projects, link_to_future_projects, options}).
- Declared success response (200): {success: true, custom_field: {id, field_type, field_name, entity_type, is_required, default_value, place_holder_text, options, applies_to_all_projects, assigned_projects, link_to_future_projects}}. Declared error shapes: 400/401/403/422/500 all share {success:false, error:{code, message, details}}.

Contract hazards captured verbatim from describeCapability guidance, worth recording even unverified:
1. field_type, field_name and is_required are all mandatory in practice even though the body schema marks nothing required. is_required must be a real JSON boolean -- the string "true" fails. Every such failure returns the identical flat 400 'Invalid Params' naming no field, so all three must be checked before retrying blind.
2. options are persisted ONLY when the same request also carries applies_to_all_projects or applies_to_all_projects or assigned_projects (the option values live on a dataset, and no dataset is built without one of those two flags/lists). Sent alone, options are silently dropped from storage while STILL being echoed back in the response -- so a dropdown can look fully configured in the API response while holding zero real values.
3. The returned custom_field object is PARTLY AN ECHO OF THE REQUEST, not a read of storage: options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects are replayed from what was sent (or defaulted false/empty), not read back. Only id, field_name, field_type, entity_type and is_required are authoritative. FLAGGING THIS PROMINENTLY: any future probe that diffs the create response against its own request body would get a false PASS on all four of those keys -- it must instead re-read the field (get_custom_field / get_custom_field_definition and its datasets) to verify against actual storage.
4. default_value cannot be set at create time for any field type -- must be set afterward via the edit capability.
5. applies_to_all_projects:true enumerates and links literally every project in the workspace, documented as stopping around 3000 projects -- the specific hazard that makes even a 'harmless-looking' create call unsafe to run casually against a real account.
6. assigned_projects takes PR-NNN identifier strings, never numeric project ids; every identifier is resolved first and one unresolvable entry fails the WHOLE call with 400 'Not all project identifiers could be found'.
7. (Also recorded from guidance, not explicitly requested but relevant): field_type can never be edited after creation -- correcting it means delete-and-recreate, which destroys all stored values; several reserved field_name values (Title, Description, Priority, State, Owner, Tags, etc.) are rejected with 400.

Comparison with siblings (index-consistency evidence): create_custom_field declares field_type values string, text, user, dropdown, multi_dropdown, url, boolean, int, date, nested_dropdown. This is the REAL vocabulary the live API returns -- confirmed directly in setup[1] above, where the 30 live rows returned field_type values string, dropdown, multi_dropdown, url, date (never text or multiselect). By contrast list_custom_fields's own declared field_type enum (text, textarea, dropdown, multiselect, number, date, boolean, url -- per a prior sibling probe recorded in tests/live/findings/list_custom_fields.md) uses text and multiselect, tokens the live API never returns in place of the real string and multi_dropdown. So create_custom_field's enum is the CORRECT entry and appears to be generated from/validated against reality, while list_custom_fields's enum appears to have inherited a stale published-spec vocabulary. This is corroborating evidence for an index-wide audit, not something this probe changes.

declared_missing and undeclared_returned are left EMPTY deliberately -- there is no invocation response to diff against, so filling either would be a guess rather than an observation. Do not backfill these without an actual invoke.

What a proper future verification would require: (a) a disposable/sandboxed account or workspace that can absorb permanent, undeletable custom-field creation without consequence (since delete_custom_field_definition is destructive-refused by the runtime and there is no other cleanup path), or an account known to be reset/torn down after the test batch; (b) verification performed against STORED state -- i.e. a follow-up get_custom_field / get_custom_field_definition (and its datasets, via get_custom_field_dataset with fetch_options=true) -- rather than trusting the create response's own echoed fields, per hazard #3 above; (c) explicit exercise of the options+assigned_projects / options+applies_to_all_projects combination to confirm dataset creation actually persists option values, since options sent alone are known (from the contract) to be silently dropped while still echoed.
